prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1437; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured's policy was reviewed and the driver listed on it is the same person who reported the collision while turning left at an intersection. Coverage was active at the time of loss, and nothing in the file points to damage predating the policy start.

Entry 2: Police confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene and recorded the impact as a left-turn collision. Responding officers noted the vehicle positions matched the reported sequence.

Entry 3: Scene photographs were obtained from the insured and show damage that is largely consistent with the described impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos are the main visual record of the event.

Entry 4: The claimant, now represented by counsel, reported a concussion following the crash. The injury described fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type.

Entry 5: Medical records show the claimant was treated in the usual manner for this kind of head injury. No prior injury to the same body area appears in the records reviewed.

Entry 6: The claimant gave the same account of the collision in every conversation so far, including the initial report and later calls with the adjuster. The sequence of events has not shifted between contacts.

Entry 7: Vehicle inspection found no sign of earlier damage to the vehicle, and the repair estimate lines up with the reported impact. The file contains no evidence of prior collisions involving this vehicle.

Entry 8: Treatment notes show the claimant's symptoms eased steadily over several weeks and the frequency of visits tapered as recovery progressed. The clinical course is consistent with a typical recovery.

Entry 9: Counsel has requested an update on the bodily injury claim and was told the file is under active review. No additional documents were submitted with the request.

Entry 10: Based on the policy confirmation, police report, photographs, medical records and vehicle inspection, the file is being handled as a standard left-turn collision claim. Next step is to finalize the injury evaluation with counsel.
